intent: Can a Roxborough Park homeowner put in a new lawn during the 2026 drought, whose rule stops it, what are their watering days, and what does the Roxborough Park Foundation require before artificial turf goes in?
distinctValue: Roxborough is unincorporated Douglas County, yet the rule against new cool-weather turf comes from the City of Aurora: Roxborough Water and Sanitation District buys its raw water from Aurora and, under its agreement with Aurora, must implement Aurora's drought restrictions. The district's Stage 1 notice (effective 7 April 2026) bans new cool-weather turf installation and enforces through a warning, then a fine on the water bill. The district's own schedule assigns watering days by neighborhood (Roxborough Park and Ravenna, Roxborough Village west or east of Rampart Range Road). Its rebates cover only washers and toilets. The Roxborough Park Foundation's governing documents turned out to be public: the Design Review Document revised 19 September 2024 defines Nonvegetative Turf Grass, says it shall not be prohibited subject to reasonable aesthetic criteria and prior approval, and sets the review steps, the seven-month completion window for landscaping changes, wildfire landscaping guidelines and the rule that natural drainage paths be preserved. The Protective Covenants put dog runs under design review and out of sight of neighbors. None of this is on the Sterling Ranch, Ken Caryl, Littleton, Highlands Ranch or Aurora pages.

Roxborough Water's Stage 1 Drought Restrictions. As you may be aware, the City of Aurora supplies water to Roxborough.

Aurora is implementing Stage 1 drought surcharges to all customers/utilities it supplies water to, including the Roxborough Water and Sanitation District. These surcharges will take effect on April 7, 2026, and remain in effect until Aurora announces that they have ended.

What This Means: Outdoor irrigation: 2 days/week on assigned days (see schedule below); No watering between 10 a.m. – 6 p.m.; No new cool-weather turf installation; Private pool filling not allowed; topping off is allowed; Decorative water features not allowed to operate
Enforcement: 1st violation: Warning. Goal is enforcement. 2nd violation: Fine applied to water bill. Repeat violations: Escalating fines and potential service interruption.
Please make a note for you and your family that this schedule begins May 1st and ends October 1st. Beginning May 1st, lawn watering is permitted 2 days per week.
You may hand-water trees, shrubs, vegetable and flower gardens on ANY day.
Free sprinkler evaluations are available through Roxborough Water's partnership with @Resource Central.
Purchase one of our last discounted Garden in A Boxes available this spring through our partner Resource Central.

Schedule graphic embedded on this page (WaterScheduleV2.png, 'KNOW YOUR SUMMER WATERING SCHEDULE'): Saturday & Wednesday: All residential homes west of Rampart Range Road in Roxborough Village. Sunday & Thursday: All residential homes east of Rampart Range Road in Roxborough Village. Including: Chatfield Acres, Chatfield East, Chatfield Estates and Plum Valley Heights. Friday & Tuesday: All residential homes in Roxborough Park and Ravenna. Monday: A permit is required to water on Mondays.

Schedule graphic: Roxborough's watering schedule is in effect May 1 - Oct 1. It allows for automatic sprinklers 2-days per week on your designated days. Violations of this schedule will result in a warning for the first time and then fines added to water bills for subsequent violations. Hand watering and drip systems are always allowed.
Schedule graphic: To get a watering permit for spring plantings, seed, or new sod, please go to the RWSD Administrative Office at 6222 N. Roxborough Park Rd. Permits are available beginning May 1.

supports: We buy our raw water from the City of Aurora and then get our contracted share of water from Strontia Springs Reservoir which is located just west of Roxborough. An agreement with the City of Aurora (revised in 2017) has secured the water for Roxborough into perpetuity.

What is the future drought response with respect to watering restrictions? Under our Agreement with Aurora, Roxborough is required to implement drought response restrictions set by the City of Aurora.

sources.label: Roxborough Park Foundation: Design Review Document (DRD), revised 19 September 2024
supports: Cover: DESIGN REVIEW DOCUMENT (DRD) Effective May 29, 2008 ... Revised: September 19, 2024. BUILDING AND LANDSCAPE DESIGN REQUIREMENTS PROCEDURES AND REGULATIONS

5.1 Definitions: "Nonvegetative Turf Grass" means synthetic simulated Turf Grass of a minimum medium pile and as approved in writing by the DRC. Outdoor carpeting, blankets, or other products that do not adequately simulate Turf Grass, as determined by the DRC, shall be prohibited.
8.15.1 and 8.15.2(6): Non-vegetative turf grass shall not be prohibited subject to reasonable aesthetic criteria and prior approval.

8.1: With the exceptions listed below, approvals from the Design Review Committee (DRC) are required when changes are made to the exterior appearance of existing structures or when landscaping changes are made, such as rock work, patios, water features or large expansions of planting beds. (The ten listed exceptions cover periodic planting, repainting in approved colors, thinning and pruning, fire-mitigation removal, dead trees, minor bed expansions, minor repairs, small shake-roof repair, like-for-like doors and windows, and deck refinishing; turf is not among them.)

2.3.2 Design Review Process: Owners shall present their plans to the committee by completing the "Request for Design Approval" form ... Renovations, additions, deletions and alterations shall require drawings, (inclusive of property line and setback designations) sketches, dimensions, color samples and property setbacks. All Request Forms, material samples, information and other specific details shall be presented to the administrative staff a minimum of three business days prior to the regularly scheduled DRC meeting.

2.3.2: Owners, their contractors, designers and architects are encouraged to meet with the DRC the afternoon of the regular scheduled meeting ... A detailed letter will be sent to the homeowner within three business days following the DRC meeting approving, disapproving or requesting additional information or clarification. ... Work shall not start until the re-submittal has received a final review and approval.
7.8: Any changes to be made to existing landscaping must be submitted and have an approved plan. The work must be completed within seven (7) months of the landscaping plan approval date.

8.15.5 Landscape Plan: the owner should call the design review coordinator at the foundation office to determine if a formal landscaping plan is required. If required, the plan shall be prepared by an overlay of the site plan (1" = 10') including all existing and proposed site grading.
5.2: Because our homes are located in the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) we are inherently at risk from wildfire.

8.15.7 Fire Mitigation Guidelines: Use earth-tone rock, gravel, and stepping stone pathways to break up the continuity of vegetation and fuels. ... Avoid organic e.g. wood mulch within five (5) feet of your house. ... Highly flammable rubber mulch shall not be used.

8.15.1 landscape planning items: Existing natural drainage paths shall be preserved. ... Conserve and protect trees, shrubs, topsoil, rock formations and unique landscape features. ... Avoid creating large, manicured areas.

sources.label: Roxborough Park Foundation: Protective Covenants
supports: Section 5.8 Restrictions on Animals and Pets: All dog runs, kennels and enclosed areas for the confinement of permitted animals shall be subject to design review and be maintained in a location not visible from any other Lot, Unit, Common Area or the Golf Course.

Section 5.7 Landscaping Requirements and Restrictions. The landscaping of each Lot, Unit, Commercial Area, Golf Course or Project Area shall be maintained by the Owner in a neat, attractive and well-kept condition.

This searchable transcription is of the Amended and Restated Protective Covenants, recorded 2004 12 02 (file name: '...2004 12 02 ..._SIGNED_&_RECORDED.pdf'); the Section 5.8 dog-run wording matches the recorded 2004 document word for word.
